notes.4ii: Candidates were confident in their use of the scalar product apart from occasional errors when multiplying by 0. The solution of p² = 64 was often given as p = 8, rather than p = ±8.
notes.6i: This question caused most candidates difficulty with only a small proportion of candidates being able to use similar triangles to express y in terms of x. Others chose to find the equation of the line ST and were more successful. Surprisingly, even when y was given in terms of x, many candidates did not realise that the area of the rectangle was xy. At least a quarter of all solutions attempted to express the area of the rectangle as “96 – the sum of the areas of triangles SRQ and QPT”. The candidates who did not equate this with “xy” were unable to make further progress.
notes.7i: Use of the formula for the nth term was well done, but misuse of units (minutes and seconds) led to many incorrect answers.
notes.7b: This question was very well answered with most candidates scoring full marks. Finding r = instead of was a common error and one which should have been checked since the sum to infinity only exists for │r│< 1.
notes.8ii: Only about a half of all solutions offered the end-points of −5 and 1, and many of these used inequality signs incorrectly; x < −5 and x < 1 being a typical incorrect answer.
notes.8iii: The sketch graphs were generally well drawn, though many candidates wasted a lot of time in producing accurate graphs, rather than sketch graphs. Many examples were seen in which the graphs were either straight lines or parabolic in shape. It was rare to see the curve “flattening” at x = 0 and x = 2π.
notes.8iv: Only a small proportion of solutions to the inverse of the function were fully correct.
notes.8v: The responses to this part of the question were excellent. Apart from the occasional algebraic error and leaving the answer in terms of y rather than x, full marks were nearly always awarded.
notes.9i: The majority of candidates recognised the need to find the value of at x = 1 and multiply by 0.04 (the rate of change of x with respect to t).
notes.key_messages: • Attention needs to be paid to making sure workings are carried out at a sufficient level of accuracy to ensure the accuracy of the final answer. • Candidates need to be careful to eliminate arithmetic and numerical errors in their answers. General Comments This paper covered the whole breadth of the syllabus and for those candidates who had covered the syllabus thoroughly and had practised by answering previous papers, it gave the opportunity to achieve high marks.
